would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh sets `set -euo pipefail` (line 24). WS_ROOT is defined only inside hive-launch, never in the drill's own shell (the drill exports HIVE_TMUX_SESSION, WS_HUB, OPS_WS, CANON_ROOT, WORK_ROOT, WRAPPER_DIR at lines 151-157, and never sources hive-common.sh in the main shell). The operator who runs the drill against the green cell — the exact hand-off the rubric describes — gets `hive-tooling-drill.sh: line 190: WS_ROOT: unbound variable` and a non-zero exit immediately after the alpha-demo launch section. Confirmed by running the same construct: `set -euo pipefail; foo -c "$WS_ROOT"` exits 1 with `WS_ROOT: unbound variable`. Both order scope item 4 clauses fail: the occupied-index case and the half-launch recovery assertion never execute, and the existing assertions do not stay green. The 'after' half of the reproduction evidence, which the report defers to this operator run, is therefore unreachable. bash -n and shellcheck cannot catch this class (both verifier logs are empty/clean), so it would have reached the operator undetected.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence:
artefacts/scripts/hive-launch:234 (`cat >&2 <<RECOVERY`, unquoted delimiter) with lines 256-261; reproduced by extracting manual_completion verbatim and running it, which prints:
  HIVE_KICKOFF=$KICKOFF
  tmux new-window -a -t 'hive' -n 'alpha-demo' -c '...' \
    -e HIVE_KICKOFF="" 'claude "$HIVE_KICKOFF"'
The multi-line kickoff heredoc is gone and the -e value is empty. The result report claims the opposite: artefacts/workspace.patch:36-38 ("prints the tmux error, the filled kickoff, the wrapper, and a copy/paste manual completion command") and RUNBOOK text at artefacts/workspace.patch:15-17 ("Use the launcher's printed filled kickoff and remaining tmux command").
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The half-launch recovery print is emitted from an unquoted here-document, so the copy/paste completion command is evaluated at print time and collapses to `HIVE_KICKOFF=$KICKOFF` plus `tmux new-window ... -e HIVE_KICKOFF=""` — pasting it creates the task window with an empty kickoff.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: Scope item 3 exists so that a post-seeding window failure converts into a documented manual finish. The operator hitting that failure is told by the launcher and by the new RUNBOOK paragraph to use the printed tmux command; running it verbatim succeeds and creates a correctly named window, but the worker starts with no prompt at all (HIVE_KICKOFF is empty), so the board still says assigned while the worker has no task and no instructions. The failure is silent — the window exists, so it reads as a completed recovery — which reproduces the stranded/archaeology state the order was written to eliminate. The nested `$(cat <<'HIVE_KICKOFF_TEXT' ... )` block the author intended to print literally is executed by the launcher instead of shown, and `-e HIVE_KICKOFF="$HIVE_KICKOFF"` expands against a variable the launcher never sets (its variable is KICKOFF). Neither mechanical check catches this: `bash -n` and `shellcheck -x` are both clean (verifier/bash-syntax.log, verifier/shellcheck.log are empty), and the new drill assertions only grep for the `----- filled kickoff -----` marker and the wrapper path (artefacts/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh, the two `check "half-launch prints ..."` lines), both of which still pass on the corrupted output.
